stimulus.text:
Black population of selected northern cities, 1910 and 1920:

| City | Black population, 1910 | Black population, 1920 |
| New York | 91,709 | 152,467 |
| Philadelphia | 84,459 | 134,229 |
| Chicago | 44,103 | 109,458 |
| Detroit | 5,741 | 40,838 |
| Cleveland | 8,448 | 34,451 |

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, as reported by the National Park Service.
stimulus.source_note: Data: U.S. Census Bureau, Black population of selected cities, 1910 and 1920, as reported by the National Park Service.

source: original; stimulus data from the U.S. Census Bureau, as reported by the National Park Service
stem: Which city in the table grew fastest in percentage terms between 1910 and 1920?

options.misconception: New York grew from 91,709 to 152,467, an increase of about two-thirds, not the fastest rate.
Chicago grew from 44,103 to 109,458, more than doubling, but Detroit grew far faster.
Philadelphia grew from 84,459 to 134,229, an increase of about three-fifths.

rationales.A: New York grew from 91,709 to 152,467, an increase of about two-thirds, not the fastest rate.
rationales.B: Chicago grew from 44,103 to 109,458, more than doubling, but Detroit grew far faster.
rationales.C: Philadelphia grew from 84,459 to 134,229, an increase of about three-fifths.
rationales.D: Detroit grew from 5,741 to 40,838, more than seven times its 1910 size, the fastest rate in the table.
rationales.general:
1. Compare each city's growth as a multiple of its 1910 size, not just in people added.
2. Detroit went from 5,741 to 40,838, more than seven times larger. No other city came close.
3. Note the lesson: the fastest rate belongs to the city that started smallest.
Remember: fastest growth in percentage terms is a ratio, so divide the new number by the old one.
